settings.title: Metaphorum 2026
settings.tagline: 100 Years of Stafford Beer - Metaphorum Conference 2026

children.text: Applications of the Viable System Model in organisations, governance and software: case studies, diagnostics and design work grounded in Stafford Beer's organisational cybernetics.
Complexity approaches to sustainability, self-governance and the Sustainable Development Goals — from eco-communities to national environmental policy.
Designing adaptive, resilient organisations: identity, variety engineering, disaster response and the tools cybernetics offers for turbulent environments.

data.title: Opening Keynote: Cybernetics for a World in Crisis

children.text: One hundred years after Stafford Beer's birth, the problems he devoted his life to — governing complex systems under accelerating change — have only grown more urgent. This opening keynote frames the conference themes and asks what organisational cybernetics has to offer a world facing climate breakdown, institutional distrust and runaway technology.
We will revisit Beer's insistence that viability is a property of whole systems, and trace a path from the Chilean Cybersyn project to today's experiments in sustainable self-governance.

data.title: The Viable System Model in Water Governance: Lessons from Brazil

children.text: Water governance is a paradigmatic complex adaptive system: many stakeholders, nested jurisdictions, and feedback loops that cross ecological and institutional boundaries. This session reports on applying the Viable System Model to state water resource councils in Brazil.

We examine how VSM diagnosis exposed missing coordination functions between basin committees and state agencies, and how recursive design helped rebalance autonomy and cohesion across levels of governance.

data.title: The Ibex Identity Model: Surprise Metabolism and Recursive Closure

children.text: How does an organisation know what it is — and how does that identity survive contact with a surprising world? The Ibex Identity Model integrates surprise metabolism, recursive closure and cybernetic stewardship into a single framework for organisational identity.

Drawing on control systems engineering and decades of research practice, this session shows how organisations can metabolise surprise rather than suppress it, turning perturbation into structural learning.

data.title: Complexity Management in Transition: Lessons from Cambodia

children.text: Transition management assumes institutions capable of steering; in fast-developing economies those institutions are themselves in flux. This session draws on projects in Cambodia to explore how complexity-inspired management systems can support strategy, security and sustainability where formal structures are still co-evolving.
Cases span higher education, innovation programmes and public administration across the UK, Europe, Latin America and South-East Asia.

data.title: Leadership and Workforce Psychology for the SDGs

children.text: Sustainability targets are set at the level of nations, but they are met — or missed — inside organisations, by people. This session connects leadership research and workforce psychology with the Sustainable Development Goals, drawing on a decade of teaching and consulting in the Gulf region.
We discuss how management education aligned with UN-PRME can build the variety leaders need to hold both commercial and ecological goals.

data.title: Sustainable Self-Governance with the Viable System Model

children.text: Can businesses and societies govern themselves sustainably — without waiting for hierarchy to save them? Building on 'A Complexity Approach to Sustainability' and 'Sustainable Self-governance in Businesses and Societies', this session presents the VSM as a practical method for self-organisation.
Examples range from Colombian regional programmes to European community enterprises, tracing three decades of action research with the model Stafford Beer left us.

data.title: Forty Years of the VSM in Cooperatives and Eco-Communities

children.text: Cooperatives promise democratic work — and routinely drown in meetings. This session distils forty years of using the Viable System Model to give co-ops and eco-communities structure without bosses: clear operational autonomy, light-touch coordination, and meta-systemic functions that members actually understand.
Includes work with the Transition Network, the Permaculture Association and the Cooperative Group.

data.title: Managing Spontaneous Volunteers in Disasters: A VSM Approach

children.text: When disaster strikes, thousands of volunteers converge — unrequested, unregistered and indispensable. Emergency management doctrine treats them as a problem; this research treats them as variety the response system must absorb.
Using the VSM and soft systems methodology, we model how response organisations can integrate spontaneous volunteers while preserving safety, accountability and their own viability.

data.title: Team Syntegrity and the Operations Room

children.text: Stafford Beer designed protocols as carefully as he designed models. This session revisits two of them from the perspective of twenty years of practice: Team Syntegrity as a non-hierarchical protocol for collective decision, and the Operations Room as an environment for real-time management.
We look at what survives contact with nonprofit boards, what needed adaptation, and what a digital-era operations room might look like.

data.title: VSMod®: Software Support for the Viable System Method

children.text: Diagnosing an organisation with the VSM produces a wealth of interconnected judgements that quickly outgrow whiteboards. VSMod® is a software environment developed to support the Viable System Method end to end — from recursion analysis to diagnosis and design.
The session demonstrates the tool on real cases and discusses how software can make cybernetic diagnosis teachable, repeatable and shareable.

data.name: Juliana Mariano Alves
data.abstract: Applies the Viable System Model to complex adaptive systems, particularly water governance in Brazil.

children.text: Universidade Estadual do Tocantins

Professor at Universidade Estadual do Tocantins, where she leads the Research Group on Development and Environmental Performance. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, a Master's degree in Agroecosystems, and a Ph.D. in Regional Development. She has been a Visiting Researcher at the Institute of Management and Strategy, University of St. Gallen, Switzerland. She has provided consultancy to the Ministry of the Environment of Brazil and the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture. She is a board member of the State Council for Water Resources in Brazil, Ambassador of the Climate Solutions Simulator of MIT, and board member of Metaphorum and the American Society for Cybernetics. Her work focuses on applying the Viable System Model (VSM) to complex adaptive systems, particularly in water governance.

data.name: Steve Brewis
data.abstract: Systems thinker and developer of the Ibex Identity Model, integrating surprise metabolism and cybernetic stewardship.

children.text: The Infinite Game

CEO of The Infinite Game and systems thinker with a background in telecommunications, control systems engineering, and organizational design. Former Chief Research Scientist at BT and Project Supervisor at the University of Cambridge and the University of Oxford. Senior Researcher at Khalifa University and Lecturer at the University of Northumbria. Developer of the Ibex Identity Model and frameworks integrating surprise metabolism, recursive closure, and cybernetic stewardship. Chartered Engineer (CEng) and Honorary Fellow of The Cybernetics Society.

data.name: Pedro Pablo Cardoso
data.abstract: Researcher in complexity in management, leading projects across the UK, Europe, Latin America, and Cambodia.

children.text: University of Exeter / De Montfort University

Honorary Senior Lecturer at the University of Exeter and Programme Director at De Montfort University (Cambodia). Consultant and researcher in complexity in management, with previous roles at Leeds Beckett University and Cranfield University. His work focuses on complexity management in strategy, security, sustainability, innovation, and management systems inspired by co-evolving and transition management principles. He has led projects across the UK, Europe, Latin America, and Cambodia.

data.name: Iffat Sabir Chaudhry
data.abstract: Works on sustainability, leadership, entrepreneurship, and workforce psychology, aligned with the SDGs.

children.text: Al Ain University, United Arab Emirates

Associate Professor of Management and Deputy Dean of the College of Business at Al Ain University, UAE. She holds a PhD in Management from the University of Hull, UK. With over a decade of experience in the UAE and Oman, her work focuses on sustainability, leadership, entrepreneurship, and workforce psychology. She contributes to UN-PRME Youth Talks and the PRME Mentorship Program, aligning her teaching with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

data.name: Angela Espinosa
data.abstract: Director of Metaphorum and organizational cybernetics scholar; worked closely with Stafford Beer.

children.text: Metaphorum

Director of Metaphorum and organizational cybernetics scholar. She earned her PhD in organizational cybernetics in 1995 and worked closely with Stafford Beer. Former Reader in Cybernetics at Hull University Business School and currently an Emeritus Fellow. Honorary Research Fellow at Exeter University and Transylvania Executive Education. Recipient of the Ashby Lecture (2002) and Norbert Wiener Award (2006). Author of books including 'A Complexity Approach to Sustainability' and 'Sustainable Self-governance in Businesses and Societies: The Viable System Model in Action'.

data.name: Jon Walker
data.abstract: Pioneered the use of the Viable System Model in cooperatives and eco-communities over forty years.

children.text: Metaphorum

Director at Metaphorum with over forty years of experience in the cooperative business sector. He has established and co-managed multiple businesses and pioneered the use of the Viable System Model in cooperatives and eco-communities. Co-author of 'A Complexity Approach to Sustainability' with Angela Espinosa. He works with the Transition Network, the Permaculture Association, and the Cooperative Group, and consults internationally on complexity and cybernetics.

data.name: Ayham Fattoum
data.abstract: Researches resilience and viability of systems during emergencies, particularly spontaneous volunteers in disasters.

children.text: University of Manchester

Lecturer in Management Studies and Operational Disaster Management at the University of Manchester. He holds a PhD in Business and Management (Operations Management) from Alliance Manchester Business School and an MSc from the University of Warwick. His research focuses on enhancing resilience, agility, and viability of systems during emergencies, particularly managing spontaneous volunteers in disasters, using VSM, SSM, and systems thinking methodologies.

data.name: Allenna Leonard
data.abstract: Worked with Stafford Beer for two decades; applies the VSM, Team Syntegrity, and Operations Room design.

children.text: Cwarel Isaf Institute

Principal at Cwarel Isaf Institute and independent consultant based in Toronto. She worked with Stafford Beer from the early 1980s until his death in 2002. Former President of Metaphorum, the American Society for Cybernetics, and the International Society for Systems Science. She applies cybernetic approaches including the Viable System Model, Team Syntegrity, and Operations Room design in nonprofit and business organizations.

data.name: Jose Manuel Perez Rios
data.abstract: Creator of the VSMod® software supporting the Viable System Model; specialist in system dynamics and organizational cybernetics.

children.text: University of Valladolid, Spain

Professor at the University of Valladolid specializing in system dynamics and organizational cybernetics. Creator of the VSMod® software supporting the Viable System Model. Former Director of International Relations at the University of Valladolid (2000–2006). Author of over 80 publications and five books, including 'Design and Diagnosis for Sustainable Organizations: The Viable System Method'. Recipient of the Kybernetes Research Award (2006) and Honorary HSSS Award as Distinguished Scientist (2007). Board member of the World Organization of Systems and Cybernetics and Fellow of HSSS.
